'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day

{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>

{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

revision.text:
{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. '''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day

{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11526135]] Wikidata name: Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:57, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2024th year 9月 | 独自研究 = 2024th year 9月 }} [[File:Aomori Nebuta Festival Float August 2006.jpg|thumb|250px|[[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Festival]] (青森市)]] [[File:Hiru kanto 1.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田市)]] [[File:Sendai Tanabata 2005.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (仙台市)]] {{GeoGroup}}
'''Tohoku Sandai Matsuri''' (東北三大祭り) refers to the three major summer festivals of the [[:en:Tōhoku region|Tōhoku region]], namely the {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}}, the {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}}. It is unclear when this term first came into use, but it became widely known after the Japanese National Railways (JNR) began promoting the festivals through the sale of special {{ill|Tourist Round Trip Tickets|ja|回遊券|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Round Trip Tickets|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1958. This campaign popularized the term and established the festivals as key attractions of Tōhoku.<ref>東北都市学会『東北都市事典』2004th year , 269-270頁。</ref>
This article also covers other festival combinations beyond the "three major festivals."
== Overview == The major summer festivals of Tōhoku are concentrated in early August, with their schedules overlapping significantly. This makes them convenient to combine into summer [[:en:Package tour|Package tours]] offered by travel agencies. As a result, the term "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" has gained traction as a brand name for tour products (though not trademarked). The specific number and combination of festivals are flexible and often tailored to the needs of consumers.
The Tōhoku region is geographically expansive, roughly the size of the [[:en:Chūbu region|Chūbu region]], with a north-south distance making travel distances substantial. However, improvements in transportation infrastructure—such as the construction of national highways, expressways (e.g., {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東北自動車道}}, {{ill|Yamagata Expressway|ja|山形道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山形自動車道}}, and {{ill|Akita Expressway|ja|秋田道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Expressway|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 秋田自動車道}}), the opening of [[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] lines (e.g., [[:en:Tōhoku Shinkansen|Tōhoku Shinkansen]], [[:en:Yamagata Shinkansen|Yamagata Shinkansen]], and [[:en:Akita Shinkansen|Akita Shinkansen]]), and the development of regional airports—have made it possible to tour Tōhoku in a short period. This has led to the emergence of various "N-dai" combinations, ranging from "two major" to "six major" festivals.
The current "Tohoku N-dai (Summer) Festivals" are closely tied to tourism models that combine sightseeing in Tōhoku with experiencing its vibrant summer festivals. This diversity has encouraged regional tourism boards to propose various optional tours featuring different combinations of festivals.
Each festival also serves as a cultural representative for its respective prefecture, participating in Japanese cultural events abroad and domestic exhibitions, such as "Japan Week" (hosted by the International Friendship Association), {{ill|Tohoku Rokkonsai|ja|東化六魂祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Rokkonsai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (rotating across Tōhoku's six prefectural capitals), and {{ill|Onagori Festival|ja|おなごりフェスティバル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onagori Festival|qq=}} (in Noshiro, Akita Prefecture). == Tōhoku N-dai Festivals == === Tōhoku Sandai Festivals === {{GeoGroup|section=東北三大祭り}} The "Three Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" generally consist of the following three festivals:<ref>[https://www.asahi.com/kids/kotoba/TKY200707250429.html 東北三大祭りとは何？] (朝日小学生新聞, July 25, 2007)</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り 観客分散、観覧席削減...感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Festival|ja|仙台七夕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仙台七夕}} (宮城県 仙台市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 684,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Festival|ja|青森ねぶた祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori Nebuta Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 青森ねぶた}} (青森県 青森市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 532,000 visitors per day * {{ill|Akita Kantō|lt=Akita Kantō Festival|ja|秋田章燕まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akita Kantō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (秋田県 秋田市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 335,000 visitors per day
These festivals share several commonalities:
* Origins: All three are rooted in customs related to [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]], particularly rituals for warding off sleep demons like "Nemuri Nagashi" (Drowsiness Flow). * Established Festivals: Each festival had solidified its format before World War II. * Locations: Hosted in prefectural capitals. * Visitors: Among the top three in daily attendance (excluding fireworks festivals).
=== Tōhoku Yondai Festivals === The "Four Major (Summer) Festivals of Tōhoku" include the above three festivals and the {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These festivals are held in prefectural capitals and had solidified their formats by the period of Japan's rapid economic growth.
* {{ill|Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|ja|山形花布祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Hanagasa Festival|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (山形県 山形市, [[:en:Coordinate system|Coordinates]]): 303,000 visitors per day
== Features == * The summer festivals in Tōhoku are celebrated with heightened enthusiasm, particularly in northern areas. * For tourists from western Japan or the Kanto region, the cooler summer temperatures in Tōhoku provide an escape from the heat. * Recent trends show increased popularity for Aomori's summer festivals due to their vibrant performances. * The economic ripple effect of Tōhoku's summer festivals was estimated in 2007 as follows: Aomori Nebuta (49.7 billion yen), Sendai Tanabata (33.2 billion yen), and Akita Kanto (19.5 billion yen).<ref name="shonaibank">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsi.co.jp/report/research/2007/festival0822.pdf|東北六大祭りの経済動向}}</ref>
